minor.issue: 2019;59(6):1001-1010 cannot be verified from the source, which is the online-first version (2018 Aug 28, DOI 10.23736/S0022-4707.18.08879-5).
A single sentence with no study count (11 studies: 3 RCTs, 1 cohort, 4 case series, 3 case reports), no population and no statement that pooling was impossible.
No numbers at all (e.g., 23 vs 4 returned in Holmich; 12.8 vs 17.3 weeks in Weir), and it omits that return rate and pain resolution did not differ between the MMT and ET groups.
The advice on classifying the presentation and on change-of-direction tolerance criteria is reasonable, but it is generic clinical reasoning rather than findings of the review.
It calls Holmich's work '2 randomized trials', but it is one RCT (1999) plus its 8-12-year follow-up (2011). The 23 (79%) vs 4 (14%) figures come from the 1999 trial.
'helped athletes ... return to sport' is somewhat causal for evidence that is mostly case series and reports, although the sentence goes on to hedge on quality.

Google and Google Scholar are presented as grey literature. That matches the body text, but the paper's abstract lists them among the searched databases, which is a minor inconsistency in the source that B does not mention.

note: B's numbers (383 screened, 11 included, 79% vs 14%, 12.8 vs 17.3 weeks, 89%/100%, 38/44, 10/38 recurrence) all check against the source, while A is accurate but thin and gives no data.
